Radviliskis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiaulių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Radviliskis grew rapidly after becoming a large railway junction in the early 19th century, and unlike most communities in this collection, actually avoided significant WWI-era emigration — the war itself, via German-imported Jewish labor from Vilna and hundreds of military supply trains, brought economic opportunity rather than hardship. On July 12, 1941, all the town's Jewish men were shot and buried in a grove next to this cemetery; women and children were sent to the Siauliai ghetto or to Žagarė, documented elsewhere in this collection, where most died alongside that town's own Jews. Until the end of the 19th century, Radviliskis's Jews had no cemetery of their own. After the war, this site became difficult to access after a private farm owner fenced his land without leaving a path to it — a problem the local municipality only resolved in 2018.
